topic: Semaglutide and tirzepatide for obesity: weight-loss efficacy in clinical trials and main safety concerns

key_points.point: In the Wegovy label's 68-week obesity trial (STEP 1 per published literature; label calls it Study 2), semaglutide 2.4 mg gave -14.9% vs -2.4% placebo; 83.5% lost at least 5% and 47.9% at least 15%.
SURMOUNT-1 (2,539 adults without diabetes, 72 weeks): tirzepatide 5/10/15 mg gave mean -16.0/-21.4/-22.5% vs -2.4% placebo; 89-96% lost at least 5% weight versus 27.9% on placebo.
Head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 (751 adults with obesity, no diabetes, 72 weeks): tirzepatide produced 20.2% mean weight loss versus 13.7% with semaglutide, with similar GI-dominated safety profiles.
Gastrointestinal events are the most common adverse reactions: with semaglutide 2.4 mg nausea 44% (placebo 16%), diarrhea 30%, vomiting 24%, constipation 24%; mostly during dose escalation.
Discontinuation for adverse events in SURMOUNT-1 was 4.3% (5 mg), 7.1% (10 mg), 6.2% (15 mg) versus 2.6% on placebo.

Both Wegovy and Zepbound carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors (seen in rodents; human relevance unknown) and are contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

Wegovy label warnings include acute pancreatitis, acute gallbladder disease, acute kidney injury from volume depletion, hypoglycemia, diabetic retinopathy complications, and pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation.

Stopping treatment leads to weight regain: after switching to placebo, SURMOUNT-4 patients regained about 14% by week 88 and STEP 1 extension patients 11.6% by week 120, with cardiometabolic gains reversing.
EMA's PRAC concluded in June 2025 that non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) is a very rare side effect of semaglutide (up to 1 in 10,000 users); stop if confirmed.

Efficacy is lower in type 2 diabetes: the semaglutide 2.4 mg label trial in diabetes with obesity gave -9.6% vs -3.4% placebo; Wegovy also carries a MACE risk-reduction indication (HR 0.80, CI 0.72-0.90).
Tirzepatide acts on both GIP and GLP-1 receptors (commentators credit this for greater loss than semaglutide); Zepbound was FDA-approved for chronic weight management on 8 Nov 2023.
Pivotal trials were manufacturer-sponsored, ran 68-72 weeks with lifestyle support, and show wide individual variability; commentators note treatment likely needs to be long-term.
